key_insight: A spectral interface-evolution model captures fluid-fluid displacement in rough fractures beyond the quasistatic limit, showing that viscosity changes the relaxation time of Haines jumps but not the total dissipated energy.
engineering_relevance: This provides a computationally efficient route to predict hysteresis and dissipation in fractured and porous media, informing flow control and upscaling in subsurface and microfluidic systems.
method: Spectral computational approach for evolving fluid interfaces and computing energy dissipation
Validated against computational fluid dynamics simulations and experiments
Applied to a single defect and random roughness to probe multiscale dynamics
evidence_signal: The abstract reports validation by comparison with CFD simulations and experiments, and demonstrates efficient tracking over many orders of magnitude in time.
watch_item: The approach is demonstrated on a model rough Hele-Shaw fracture, so extension to fully 3D or more complex porous geometries may require further validation.
paper_title: Dynamics of fluid-fluid displacements in a model rough fracture beyond the quasistatic limit: A spectral approach
